content: Kaohsiung Medical University, previously known as Kaohsiung Medical College, is a private university situated in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. It is widely regarded as the premier institution for research and education in the Kaohsiung region. Kaohsiung Medical College was established in 1954 by Frank C. Chen, a former mayor of Kaohsiung, who donated land from the city for the college, and Professor Tu Tsung-ming, Taiwan's first Doctor of Medicine. Upon its founding, it became the first private medical institution of its kind in Southern Taiwan. Professor Tu, the college's first president, was committed to advancing the institution with his guiding principles: Joyfully embracing learning, putting research first and Resolutely striving for progress, encouraging study, and benefiting the world. In August 1999, the college was officially renamed Kaohsiung Medical University with approval from Taiwan's Ministry of Education. This transformation was aimed at addressing the increasing internationalization of society and adapting to the evolving challenges of the modern era. The university has consistently received superior ratings in all categories under the Ministry of Education's Mid-term School Administration Development Plan. Three years after its establishment, the college founded its hospital in June 1957, now known as the Chung-Ho Memorial Hospital, Kaohsiung Medical University. This hospital has grown to become the largest medical center in Southern Taiwan. It not only trains students and faculty but also provides essential healthcare services to the region, fulfilling its threefold mission of teaching, research, and service. In 1998, the university entered into an agreement with the Kaohsiung Municipal Government to take over the management of Hsiao-kang Hospital, which continues to deliver medical care and community health services. The university boasts a teacher-student ratio of 1:12, surpassing the standards set by Taiwan's Ministry of Education. With private funding and government subsidies, the institution is able to implement diverse employment programs to attract outstanding scholars and educators from both Taiwan and abroad. Additionally, up to 35 million New Taiwan dollars are allocated annually for scholarships and student grants. Kaohsiung Medical University is recognized as a leading center for medical research in Southern Taiwan, with a strong team of highly qualified and experienced researchers. The university operates four university-level research centers, six focal research centers, and 20 interdisciplinary research teams, comprising experts from various fields. It actively promotes interdisciplinary research and fosters collaboration between teams working on basic research and its clinical applications. The university's MedicoGenomic Research Center has successfully developed diagnostic chips for colorectal cancer and identified molecular markers (both DNA and RNA) for tumors, which can be utilized in laboratory and clinical settings. The Functional Proteomics Research Center conducts systematic studies on cellular proteins, including their types, functions, expression differences, and post-translational modifications. Meanwhile, the Chinese Herbal Medicine and New Drug Research Center is focused on creating innovative drug models for herbal medicines and developing herbal prescriptions that meet international standards.
